key_insight: A short shared coupler suppresses symmetric-mode torsional loss, enabling coupled square resonators to exceed the dissipation dilution of an isolated polygon.
engineering_relevance: Coupler geometry provides a design lever for tuning frequency splitting and mechanical loss in coupled resonators.
method: Develop a continuum model of two identical square resonators joined by a shared tether.
Relate coupler length and width to mode splitting and dissipation dilution, and compare with finite element simulations.
Derive Q·f scaling in the short-coupler and short-supporting-tether limits.
evidence_signal: For a 100 μm-long, 2 μm-wide coupler, finite element calculations predict 17.7 Hz frequency splitting and symmetric-mode dilution approximately 13% above the analytical isolated-polygon value.
watch_item: The reported validation is numerical, and the asymptotic loss suppression and Q·f expression require short-coupler or short-tether conditions.
paper_title: Coupled Soft-Clamped Polygon Resonators with Tunable Mechanical Coupling
